transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-07-28 15:00 UTC
Duration: 38 mins
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Halite Head of Platform), Ethan Moore (CTO), Lena Park (SRE), Omar Diaz (Product)

Summary: quick discovery — PLG quickstart, free credits, time-to-first-token, security controls, hosted vs dedicated vs private options discussed.

00:00 Alyssa: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — um, quick intros. I'm Alyssa, AE on the PLG team, and Marco's our solutions engineer.
00:10 Priya: Hi, Priya here, head of platform at Halite. We're looking to add LLM features centrally, want low friction for product teams.
00:18 Ethan: Ethan, CTO. Big concerns: latency, costs, and of course data controls.
00:25 Marco: Awesome. Quick outline: we'll run through the self-serve quickstart, what free credits look like, then map to hosted/dedicated/private paths and what triggers a move.
01:05 Priya: Our main ask — fastest time-to-first-token for internal teams, ideally under a day to get a working prototype. Also need to understand how tokens are metered and retention.
01:22 Alyssa: Yep, that's the PLG flow. We give free credits, a quickstart repo, and SDKs. Typically teams get a token in under an hour if they follow the quickstart, sometimes minutes with the right API key and CORS setup. We'll send the quickstart link after.
02:05 Marco: On the API side we have REST and SDKs, streaming, function calling. For quick PoC, folks use hosted API. Dedicated is reserved capacity for predictable throughput; Private is VPC/on-prem for compliance.
02:42 Lena: On Private — how's KMS handled? We need customer-managed keys for certain data sets.
02:50 Marco: Yes, Private supports KMS/HSM integrations, and you can bring your own keys. For Dedicated we also support envelope encryption with KMS.
03:15 Ethan: Can you summarize the main tradeoffs — latency and cost? If we keep hosted, what's typical p95 latency?
03:30 Marco: For the smaller models on hosted we typically see p95 around 150-250ms token-gen on our benchmarks, larger models higher. Dedicated gives you pinned GPUs which reduces variance and tail latency. There's a cost delta — dedicated is contracted capacity.
04:05 Priya: And caching — does Redwood do prefix or KV cache automatically? That matters for cost.
04:12 Marco: Yes, automatic prefix caching / KV cache is part of the runtime. It helps a lot for assistant-style workloads.
04:35 Omar: We currently use OpenAI for prototypes. We're curious how easy switching is and whether the SDKs and prompts port cleanly.
04:50 Alyssa: Pretty straightforward — our API is similar for basic generation and embeddings. We'll share migration notes. Also, quick note: some transcriptions mis-say our own feature names, but the doc will have correct names.
05:20 Priya: Security: SOC2? ISO? Audit logs? We need detailed docs before we talk to procurement.
05:30 Alyssa: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO compliance docs, audit logs, RBAC, SSO/SAML, and detailed network diagrams. I'll share the security whitepaper link.
06:05 Ethan: Data residency — we have EU customers and certain datasets can't leave region. Is hosted available in multiple regions?
06:16 Marco: Hosted has multi-region options; we can route by region, but for strict residency the Private deployment (VPC) is the recommended path. Dedicated also can be region pinned.
06:40 Priya: For a quickstart pilot, we'd prefer hosted universal, then move to Dedicated if cost / latency / compliance require. Typical timeline?
06:50 Alyssa: Many customers pilot for 4-8 weeks. For a ramp to Dedicated or Private, plan for 6-12 weeks to provision and test.
07:10 Omar: Free credits question — are those tied to account only, or can we split across teams?
07:20 Alyssa: Free credits are applied at the account/org level and we have tooling to allocate to subteams. We'll include instructions.
07:42 Priya: One of our SREs — Lena — asked about observability: token-level cost breakdown, tracing hooks, and per-route dashboards.
07:55 Marco: Redwood Console has per-route model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns and trace integration. We can show a quick console tour in the follow-up demo.
08:30 Ethan: Any hard limits on concurrency? We have bursty workloads.
08:38 Marco: On hosted there are rate limits; for production-level burst you bump to Dedicated or request temporary burst capacity. Dedicated configs are flexible with autoscaling and burst options.
09:05 Priya: For Private, how does deployment lifecycle work? Upgrades, rollouts, canaries?
09:15 Marco: Private supports the same rollout primitives — canaries, A/B, automatic fallback to older pinned models. The control plane is customer-managed in most Private setups.
09:45 Omar: Do you support quantized models for cost savings?
09:52 Marco: Yes, our runtime has quantization-friendly execution and we provide model recommendations per workload; we'll include a quantization primer.
10:20 Priya: Latency SLOs — we need 99th < 800ms for user-facing chat. Is that achievable hosted?
10:35 Marco: For smaller context lengths and optimized kernels yes; but 99th depends on model choice and traffic pattern. For strict 99th SLOs Dedicated is safer. We'll map expected percentiles for your token sizes once we see sample prompts.
11:10 Priya: Ok — what do you need from us to get started with a quick pilot?
11:20 Alyssa: Minimum: a single developer, sample prompts / prompt set, expected token volumes, target SLOs, and a point of contact for security. We'll issue free credits and share quickstart repo.
12:05 Ethan: How fast can a dev get a token if they follow the quickstart? We want to show product teams something this week.
12:12 Alyssa: Usually within 30-60 minutes: sign up, get API key, run example repo. If there are CORS or network blocks it can be longer. We'll provide step-by-step troubleshooting notes.
12:45 Priya: Billing model — is it per-token for hosted? Any hidden infra fees?
12:55 Alyssa: Hosted is usage-based per-token (generation/embedding rates differ). Dedicated is a commit + overage model. We'll include high-level pricing bands; for exacts we'll follow up with your expected volumes.
13:30 Omar: Procurement will want a contract and SLA for Dedicated. What does your SLA look like?
13:38 Alyssa: We offer SLA options for Dedicated with uptime and latency targets. For hosted we provide best-effort but can discuss enterprise add-ons.
14:05 Lena: Any offline/on-prem option for air-gapped environments?
14:12 Marco: We have an on-prem package for Private deployments that runs behind your firewall; it's heavier lift but supported for regulated data.
15:00 Priya: Great. Let's recap the plan.
15:07 Alyssa: Recap: we'll send quickstart and free credits, security whitepaper and network diagram, Marco will schedule a Private-focused demo and perf slides, and Halite will share token volumes and SLOs. Follow-up in two weeks for technical deep dive.
15:30 Ethan: Sounds good. Thanks all.
15:35 Alyssa: Thanks — we'll follow up with links and next steps.

End of transcript.

Shared artifacts/links: https://redwood.app/quickstart (quickstart repo), https://redwood.app/security-whitepaper (security docs), internal perf spreadsheet (shared after NDA).
